items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Oh, I've seen his greatest, he's buried out by Ron Wagamahema.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, sometime my mother would have a fish fry and she was engaged with Roy Palmer. He had a friend that played a mountain. Later on you know Roy Palmer played baritone, cornet, trombone, a lot of instruments. He was a pretty good teacher. He taught a lot of people around Chicago, including myself and Lionel Hampton and Oscar Bunny Young, who I later played with at the Wisconsin Roof for about six years. And McKinley Thomas and Baritone, we had a band around there, including the singing brothers, Homer and…

Where was Eddie Atkinson from? New Orleans. I never heard of him down here. Oh, I've seen his greatest, he's buried out by Ron Wagamahema. Did he play with bass down here? Yeah, I think so, but not in early years. In early years.
Well, I saw his picture in his family, family jazz album. Yeah, yeah. And in the uniform of brass band, you know. Yeah, the whole thing. That was a long time before he came to Chicago.
